question: Under Massachusetts law, a real estate license is generally required to engage in which of the following activities for another person, for compensation?
choice_a: Only the sale of commercial real estate; residential leasing never requires a license
choice_b: Only transactions over $1,000,000 in value
choice_c: The sale, exchange, purchase, or rental/leasing of real estate, or negotiating loans secured by a mortgage or other encumbrance on real estate
choice_d: Only transactions involving out-of-state buyers
explanation: Massachusetts law requires a license for engaging in the business of a broker or salesperson, which includes the sale, exchange, purchase, or rental/leasing of real estate, and negotiating loans secured by real estate, when performed for another for compensation.

question: Under Massachusetts law, what happens if an unlicensed person performs services as a broker and later sues in Massachusetts courts to recover compensation for those services?
choice_a: The person may always recover compensation regardless of licensure status
choice_b: The court will automatically award double damages to the unlicensed person
choice_c: Licensure status is irrelevant to a compensation claim in Massachusetts
choice_d: The person cannot recover compensation for broker services performed unless they were a duly licensed broker at the time the services were rendered
explanation: Massachusetts law bars an unlicensed person from recovering, in any suit in Massachusetts courts, compensation for services performed as a broker unless they were duly licensed at the time the services were performed.

question: Under Massachusetts law, from whom may a licensed real estate salesperson accept a fee or commission for a transaction?
choice_a: Only from their supervising licensed broker, not directly from a client or any other party
choice_b: From any party to the transaction, regardless of who employs the salesperson
choice_c: From another brokerage's salesperson working the same deal
choice_d: From the buyer only, never the seller
explanation: A Massachusetts salesperson must operate under the supervision of a licensed broker and generally may not accept compensation from anyone other than their supervising broker.

question: Under Massachusetts law, what role must a supervising broker play before a salesperson finalizes a real estate transaction?
choice_a: The broker has no role once the salesperson is licensed
choice_b: The broker must approve the negotiation and completion of the transaction by the salesperson
choice_c: Only the client's attorney may approve a transaction, not the broker
choice_d: Broker approval is required only for transactions over a certain price threshold set by the salesperson
explanation: Massachusetts law requires that a supervising broker approve the negotiation and completion of any transaction handled by a salesperson working under that broker.

question: Under Massachusetts law, which of the following is exempt from real estate broker/salesperson licensing requirements?
choice_a: A person who regularly lists and sells other people's homes for a commission but has never been licensed
choice_b: A person who negotiates the purchase of real estate on behalf of an unrelated buyer for a fee
choice_c: A property owner or the owner's regular employees performing acts of a broker with respect to the owner's own real estate
choice_d: A brokerage that advertises listings on behalf of sellers who are not its employees
explanation: Massachusetts law exempts an owner (or the owner's regular employees) who performs acts of a broker or salesperson with respect to their own property from the licensing requirement, since they are not acting for another party for compensation in the way a broker does.

question: Which of the following categories is exempt from Massachusetts real estate broker/salesperson licensing under M.G.L. c. 112, § 87QQ?
choice_a: Unlicensed sales assistants who negotiate purchase offers on a broker's behalf
choice_b: Any individual who has completed real estate coursework but has not yet passed the licensing exam
choice_c: Property management companies performing leasing activities for owners other than themselves
choice_d: Attorneys at law acting within their professional capacity, licensed auctioneers, and fiduciaries such as trustees, executors, receivers, and guardians
explanation: Massachusetts law specifically exempts attorneys acting in their professional capacity, licensed auctioneers, and various fiduciaries (trustees, executors, administrators, receivers, guardians, conservators) from the broker/salesperson licensing requirement.

question: How long is an individual Massachusetts real estate license generally valid for, under M.G.L. c. 112, § 87XX?
choice_a: It is valid until the anniversary of the licensee's date of birth occurring more than twenty-four months after the date of issuance
choice_b: It is valid for exactly one calendar year from the date of issuance with no exceptions
choice_c: It is valid permanently once issued and never requires renewal
choice_d: It is valid for five years regardless of the licensee's birthdate
explanation: Under Massachusetts law, an individual license is valid until the anniversary of the licensee's date of birth that occurs more than twenty-four months after the license was issued, effectively creating a roughly two-year term tied to the licensee's birthdate.

question: How often must a Massachusetts real estate broker or salesperson license generally be renewed?
choice_a: Annually (every year)
choice_b: Biennially (every two years)
choice_c: Every five years
choice_d: Only once, at initial licensure, with no further renewal ever required
explanation: Massachusetts real estate licenses are renewed on a biennial (two-year) cycle, consistent with the roughly two-year license term tied to the licensee's birthdate.

question: Does the Massachusetts Board require a licensee to retake the licensing examination in order to renew an existing license?
choice_a: Yes — every renewal requires passing the full licensing exam again
choice_b: Yes, but only for brokers, never for salespersons
choice_c: No — the Board renews licenses without re-examination, provided the applicant continues to meet qualifications such as good moral character
choice_d: Re-examination is required only if the licensee changed their business address
explanation: Massachusetts law provides that the Board renews licenses biennially without requiring re-examination, so long as the licensee continues to meet qualifications such as maintaining good moral character.

question: According to PSI's official Massachusetts Real Estate Examination Candidate Information Bulletin, how many hours of continuing education are required for license renewal?
choice_a: 45 hours
choice_b: 3 hours
choice_c: 24 hours
choice_d: 12 hours
explanation: Massachusetts requires 12 hours of continuing education for real estate broker and salesperson license renewal, as confirmed in PSI's official Massachusetts Candidate Information Bulletin.
source_note: PSI Massachusetts Real Estate Examination Candidate Information Bulletin (updated 09/23/2025); continuing education framework at M.G.L. c. 112, § 87XX 1/2.

question: Under Massachusetts law, licensees must certify completion of which requirement as part of their renewal, as established under M.G.L. c. 112, § 87XX 1/2?
choice_a: Completion of the required continuing education courses, certified to the Board
choice_b: Completion of a second full pre-licensing course, identical to the original
choice_c: A notarized statement of net worth
choice_d: A criminal background check renewed every renewal cycle regardless of any new offenses
explanation: Massachusetts law establishes a continuing education requirement and course completion certification process that licensees must satisfy as part of the renewal process.
source_note: M.G.L. c. 112, § 87XX 1/2 (continuing education requirements and course completion certification).

question: How far in advance of a license's expiration must the Massachusetts Board mail renewal application forms to licensees?
choice_a: At least one year before the license expires
choice_b: At least 30 days before the license expires
choice_c: The Board is not required to mail renewal forms at all
choice_d: Only 48 hours before expiration
explanation: Massachusetts law requires the Board to mail renewal application forms to licensees at least 30 days before their license is due to expire.

question: What must a Massachusetts license renewal application include, according to M.G.L. c. 112, § 87XX?
choice_a: It requires no signature, only a payment
choice_b: It must be submitted by the applicant's supervising broker instead of the applicant
choice_c: It must be signed and sworn to by the applicant and submitted on forms furnished by the Board
choice_d: It must be notarized by a Massachusetts Superior Court judge
explanation: Massachusetts law requires that a license renewal application be signed and sworn to by the applicant and made on forms furnished by the Board.

question: In addition to individual broker and salesperson licenses, Massachusetts law also provides for licensing of which type of entity, under M.G.L. c. 112, § 87UU?
choice_a: Only sole proprietorships, never corporations or partnerships
choice_b: Foreign (out-of-country) corporations exclusively
choice_c: Nonprofit organizations only
choice_d: Corporate and other organizational entities applying for a broker license
explanation: Massachusetts law provides a licensing pathway for corporate and other organizational entities to hold a broker license, distinct from individual licensure.

question: Why can a Massachusetts real estate salesperson not simply operate on their own, independent of any broker?
choice_a: Massachusetts law requires a salesperson to work under the supervision of, and be compensated through, a licensed supervising broker for all licensed activity
choice_b: There is no such restriction; salespersons may operate fully independently in Massachusetts
choice_c: Salespersons may work independently only after five years of licensure
choice_d: Independent operation is allowed only for salespersons who hold a college degree
explanation: Under Massachusetts law, a licensed salesperson's authority to act is inherently tied to a supervising broker — the salesperson must work under that broker's supervision and approval and be compensated only through the broker, rather than functioning as an independent license holder.

question: Under Massachusetts law, what must a licensee do if they change their business location?
choice_a: Nothing; business location changes need not be reported to the Board
choice_b: Promptly give written notice of the change of business location to the Board
choice_c: Notify only their clients, not the Board
choice_d: Wait until the next renewal cycle to report the change
explanation: Massachusetts law requires a licensee to promptly give the Board written notice of any change of business location.

question: What is a potential consequence under Massachusetts law for a licensee's failure to notify the Board of a change of business location?
choice_a: There is no consequence for failing to notify the Board
choice_b: A small administrative fee is the only possible consequence
choice_c: Failure to give such notice is grounds for revocation of the license
choice_d: The license automatically converts to inactive status with no further action needed
explanation: Massachusetts law expressly states that failure to give the Board written notice of a change of business location is grounds for revocation of the license, making the notification a serious, mandatory obligation.

question: After a Massachusetts licensee provides notice of a change in business location, what does the Board do?
choice_a: The Board requires the licensee to reapply from scratch, including retaking the examination
choice_b: The Board takes no further action, leaving the original license unchanged
choice_c: The Board automatically extends the license term by an additional two years
choice_d: The Board issues a replacement license reflecting the new location for the remainder of the original license term
explanation: Once a licensee provides the required notice of a change in business location, the Board issues a replacement license reflecting the new address, valid for the remainder of the original license term.

question: Under M.G.L. c. 112, § 87SS, how many classroom hours of board-approved real estate coursework must an individual complete before sitting for either the broker's or the salesperson's licensing examination?
choice_a: 40 classroom hours
choice_b: 12 classroom hours
choice_c: 75 classroom hours
choice_d: 100 classroom hours
explanation: Section 87SS requires both broker and salesperson applicants to complete board-approved courses in real estate subjects totaling 40 classroom hours of instruction before taking the applicable licensing examination.

question: Under M.G.L. c. 112, § 87SS, what real-world experience must a candidate demonstrate to qualify for a Massachusetts broker's license?
choice_a: At least 6 months of any real estate-related employment, regardless of licensure status
choice_b: Active association with a real estate broker for a period of 3 years as a real estate salesperson
choice_c: Ownership of at least one income-producing investment property
choice_d: Completion of at least 10 unsupervised transactions as an unlicensed assistant
explanation: Section 87SS requires a broker applicant to prove they have been actively associated with a real estate broker for 3 years as a licensed real estate salesperson before qualifying for a broker's license.

question: Under M.G.L. c. 112, § 87SS, what subject matter must the written licensing examination cover?
choice_a: Only state and federal fair housing case law
choice_b: Only mathematics and closing-statement calculations
choice_c: Principles of real estate practice, real estate agreements and principal-and-agent relations, and the rudimentary principles of the economics and appraising of real estate
choice_d: Only building-code and construction-inspection standards
explanation: Section 87SS specifies that the written examination must cover principles of real estate practice, real estate agreements and principal-and-agent relations, and rudimentary principles of the economics and appraising of real estate.

question: Under M.G.L. c. 112, § 87SS, at what minimum frequency must the Board administer licensing examinations each calendar year?
choice_a: Exactly once per year for each examination
choice_b: At least 12 times per year for both examinations
choice_c: Only when a minimum number of candidates has registered, with no fixed annual minimum
choice_d: At least 6 times per year for the broker's examination and at least 8 times per year for the salesperson's examination
explanation: Section 87SS requires the Board to hold broker's examinations at least six times and salesperson's examinations at least eight times in each calendar year.

question: Under M.G.L. c. 112, § 87SS, what exemption is available to a Massachusetts-licensed attorney who applies for a real estate broker's license?
choice_a: The attorney is exempt from both the written examination and the one-year residency requirement otherwise applicable to broker applicants
choice_b: The attorney is exempt only from the surety bond requirement
choice_c: The attorney is exempt from the application process entirely and receives a license automatically
choice_d: The attorney must still take the examination but may skip the 40-hour education requirement
explanation: Section 87SS exempts Massachusetts-licensed attorneys applying for a broker's license from the written examination and from the one-year residency requirement otherwise imposed on broker applicants.

question: Under M.G.L. c. 112, § 87WW, when may the Board grant a reciprocity exemption from the Massachusetts written examination to an out-of-state licensee?
choice_a: Automatically, for any applicant holding a real estate license issued by any other U.S. state
choice_b: When the applicant is a broker or salesperson already duly licensed in another state that extends similar reciprocal treatment to Massachusetts licensees
choice_c: Only if the applicant has never previously taken a licensing exam in any state
choice_d: Never; Massachusetts law contains no reciprocity provision for out-of-state licensees
explanation: Section 87WW allows the Board to exempt from the written examination a broker or salesperson already duly licensed in another state, provided that state extends a similar reciprocal exemption to Massachusetts licensees.

question: Under M.G.L. c. 112, § 87WW, is a non-resident who holds a Massachusetts real estate broker's license required to maintain an office within Massachusetts?
choice_a: Yes, maintaining a physical Massachusetts office is mandatory for every non-resident licensee
choice_b: Yes, but only once the non-resident completes more than five Massachusetts transactions in a year
choice_c: No — a non-resident broker need not maintain a Massachusetts office but must maintain a usual place of business in the state where they are licensed
choice_d: No place of business is required anywhere, in Massachusetts or the licensee's home state
explanation: Section 87WW does not require a non-resident broker to maintain an office in Massachusetts, but does require the non-resident to maintain a usual place of business in the state in which they are licensed.

question: Under M.G.L. c. 112, § 87WW, what must a non-resident applicant file with the Board before being licensed as a Massachusetts broker or salesperson?
choice_a: A certified copy of the applicant's out-of-state driver's license
choice_b: A notarized letter of recommendation from their current employer
choice_c: Federal income tax returns for the preceding three years
choice_d: A power of attorney designating the Board's chairman as the applicant's agent for service of legal process
explanation: Section 87WW requires a non-resident applicant to file a power of attorney appointing the Board's chairman as their agent for service of process, so that legal process served on the chairman is treated as if served on the non-resident directly.

question: Under M.G.L. c. 112, § 87TT, what must a corporation or partnership applying for a broker's license submit regarding its officers, directors, or partners?
choice_a: Evidence of the good moral character of all officers and directors, or holders of similar positions, or of all the partners
choice_b: Proof that each officer or partner has at least 10 years of real estate industry experience
choice_c: A unanimous board resolution waiving the entity's liability for licensee conduct
choice_d: Nothing beyond the entity's registration with the Secretary of the Commonwealth
explanation: Section 87TT requires a corporate or partnership applicant to submit evidence of the good moral character of all of its officers and directors (or holders of similar positions) or all of its partners, as applicable.

question: Under M.G.L. c. 112, § 87TT, what must an individual license applicant prove regarding citizenship?
choice_a: Massachusetts residency of at least 10 consecutive years
choice_b: United States citizenship, or present a certified declaration of intention to become a citizen
choice_c: Citizenship status is never relevant to licensure under Massachusetts law
choice_d: Dual citizenship in the United States and a second country
explanation: Section 87TT requires an individual applicant to prove United States citizenship, or, alternatively, to present a certified declaration of intention to become a citizen.

question: Under M.G.L. c. 112, § 87TT, what bond must a real estate broker applicant furnish?
choice_a: A $50,000 irrevocable letter of credit issued by a Massachusetts bank
choice_b: No bond is ever required of a Massachusetts broker applicant
choice_c: A $5,000 bond executed by the applicant and a surety company authorized to do business in Massachusetts, or by the applicant and two sufficient sureties
choice_d: A refundable $500 cash security deposit held by the Board for one year
explanation: Section 87TT requires a broker applicant to furnish a $5,000 bond, executed either by the applicant together with an authorized surety company or by the applicant together with two sufficient individual sureties, to protect aggrieved parties.

question: Under M.G.L. c. 112, § 87TT, for how long must a license application remain on file with the Board before a license may be issued?
choice_a: At least 90 days
choice_b: At least 1 full year
choice_c: There is no minimum filing period before issuance
choice_d: At least 10 days
explanation: Section 87TT requires that an application remain on file with the Board for at least ten days before a license may be issued.

question: Under M.G.L. c. 112, § 87TT, what may the Board do upon the death of a sole proprietor broker?
choice_a: Issue a temporary license to the deceased broker's legal representative, without examination, valid for up to one year and not renewable
choice_b: Automatically and permanently transfer the deceased broker's license to the legal representative
choice_c: Require the legal representative to pass the full licensing examination before any temporary authority is granted
choice_d: Take no action, requiring the brokerage to cease all operations immediately upon the broker's death
explanation: Section 87TT allows the Board to issue a temporary license, without examination, to the legal representative of a deceased sole proprietor broker, valid for up to one year and not subject to renewal.

question: Under M.G.L. c. 112, § 87UU, what must a corporation, society, association, or partnership do before it can be issued a broker's license?
choice_a: Ensure that every employee of the entity, regardless of role, individually holds a broker's license
choice_b: Designate at least one of its officers or partners as its representative, who must hold (or simultaneously apply for) an individual broker's license in their own name
choice_c: Do nothing further beyond filing its articles of organization with the Secretary of the Commonwealth
choice_d: Obtain a salesperson's license issued in the entity's own name
explanation: Section 87UU requires an entity seeking a broker's license to designate at least one officer or partner as its representative, and that representative must hold, or apply for, an individual broker's license in their own name before the entity license can issue.

question: Under M.G.L. c. 112, § 87UU, whose name or names appear on a broker's license issued to a corporation, society, association, or partnership?
choice_a: No individual names appear; only the entity's name is listed on the license
choice_b: Only the name of the entity's registered agent for service of process
choice_c: The name of each designated officer or partner who has individually been issued a broker's license
choice_d: The names of all shareholders of the entity, regardless of licensure status
explanation: Section 87UU provides that the broker's license issued to an entity bears the name of each designated officer or partner to whom an individual broker's license has been issued.

question: Under M.G.L. c. 112, § 87UU, may a salesperson's license be issued to a corporation, society, association, or partnership?
choice_a: Yes, provided the entity already holds a broker's license
choice_b: Yes, but only for entities with fewer than five employees
choice_c: Yes — salesperson's licenses are issued exclusively to entities rather than to individuals
choice_d: No — no salesperson's license shall be issued to a corporation, society, association, or partnership
explanation: Section 87UU expressly prohibits issuance of a salesperson's license to a corporation, society, association, or partnership; only individuals may hold a salesperson's license.

question: Under M.G.L. c. 112, § 87UU, may a designated licensed officer or partner of a corporate broker also act as a real estate broker on their own individual behalf?
choice_a: Only if written consent has been filed with the Board
choice_b: Yes, automatically, with no additional filing or notice required
choice_c: No, under no circumstances while affiliated with the entity
choice_d: Only after the entity itself has been formally dissolved
explanation: Section 87UU permits a designated licensed officer or partner to perform broker acts as agent or officer of the entity, but bars that individual from acting as a broker on their own personal behalf unless written consent to do so has been filed with the Board.

question: Under M.G.L. c. 112, § 87VV, may a licensed salesperson affiliated with one broker simultaneously act as a salesperson for a different licensed broker?
choice_a: Yes, as long as both brokers give written consent to the dual affiliation
choice_b: No — a licensed salesperson affiliated with a broker shall not act as a salesperson for any other licensed broker while so affiliated
choice_c: Yes, without any restriction whatsoever
choice_d: Only during the final 30 days before the salesperson's license expires
explanation: Section 87VV bars a licensed salesperson affiliated with a broker from simultaneously acting as a salesperson for any other licensed broker during that affiliation.

question: Under M.G.L. c. 112, § 87ZZ, which applicants are exempt from real estate examination and license fees?
choice_a: All applicants over the age of 65, regardless of any other characteristic
choice_b: First-time applicants only, with no other qualifying characteristic required
choice_c: Blind persons and certain honorably discharged veterans, including paraplegic veterans as defined in M.G.L. c. 115, § 6B
choice_d: No applicant is ever exempt from examination or license fees in Massachusetts
explanation: Section 87ZZ exempts blind persons and certain honorably discharged veterans, including paraplegic veterans as defined in M.G.L. c. 115, § 6B, from the examination and license fees otherwise required.

question: Under M.G.L. c. 112, § 87ZZ, how is the license issuance fee adjusted when a license is issued for less than a full license term?
choice_a: No proration ever occurs; the full biennial fee always applies regardless of the issuance date
choice_b: The fee is automatically doubled for any applicant issued a license mid-cycle
choice_c: The fee is waived entirely for the remainder of the first year
choice_d: The fee is prorated based on the number of months during which the license will be valid, with any partial month counted as a full month
explanation: Section 87ZZ requires the Board to adjust the license issuance fee based on the number of months the license will actually be valid, counting any partial month as a full month.
